findings.description: Get-ReviewCampaignVerificationSupportManifest passes frozen machinery identities directly to git ls-tree, and Add-ReviewCampaignVerificationSupport later passes the resulting names directly to git restore. Git interprets both batches as pathspecs. A legal marker-detected machinery name containing *, ?, or [] can therefore select a different tracked path. If that product path was explicitly excluded, it is absent from the snapshot, so the collision check does not stop it: the file is restored into the verification copy, can affect the command result, is removed afterward, and the post-run digest still matches target_digest. This permits green verification evidence for a composition other than the authorized candidate. Convert both batches to literal pathspecs.
findings.title: Verification support treats literal machinery identities as Git pathspecs

findings.description: ExcludedPathPatterns are normalized with Sort-Object -Unique, whose default string comparison folds case. On a case-sensitive worktree, exclusions such as Foo/** and foo/** are different authorities, but one is discarded. The discarded subtree can remain in the reviewed digest and materialized target even though the operator explicitly excluded it. Deduplicate exclusions with the filesystem-aware comparison used for path identity instead of the default PowerShell comparer.
findings.title: Case-distinct explicit exclusions are silently collapsed

findings.description: Get-ContinuousCoReviewWorktreeSourceHashes stores relative paths in a normal PowerShell hashtable, whose string keys are case-insensitive. On a case-sensitive filesystem, files such as Foo and foo overwrite the same entry. The before/after integrity comparison can therefore miss a change or deletion of the shadowed file, and source_hashes_before is not an exact candidate manifest. Use a dictionary with the resolved volume comparer and preserve distinct keys on case-sensitive volumes.
findings.title: The source integrity manifest cannot represent case-distinct files

findings.description: Set-ManagedFile reads and overwrites TargetPath without rejecting reparse points or verifying that the resolved destination remains inside the project. The new continuous-review runtime copy invokes this helper for every managed file. A project-controlled scripts/internal/continuous-co-review junction, directory symlink, or managed-file symlink can therefore redirect specrew update writes outside the project and overwrite external files. Validate the target root, every existing ancestor, and each existing target before reading or writing.
findings.title: Runtime deployment writes through untrusted links

findings.description: The volume probe declares a filesystem case-insensitive whenever a path with the directory's case-flipped name exists. On a case-sensitive filesystem that legitimately contains both Repo and REPO siblings, that test returns the wrong comparer. Downstream machinery and candidate identities can then fold distinct paths and exclude or equate the wrong content. Determine whether both spellings identify the same filesystem object, or probe lookup behavior within a controlled directory, rather than relying on alternate-name existence.
findings.title: Case-sensitivity probing mistakes a case-distinct sibling for aliasing

summary: Completed a risk-based review of candidate composition, path identity, frozen verification support, runtime deployment, parallel orchestration, and retroactive closure. Both controller verification commands succeeded against the exact target digest, but five implementation defects remain, including one approval-blocking route by which verification can run against an unauthorized composition.
